name: Gated Attention
tagline: A query-dependent sigmoid gate scales every head's attention output before the output projection.
description: The Dense Baseline's full causal attention with the G1 gate of Qiu et al.: each head's scaled dot-product attention output is multiplied elementwise by σ(X W_θ), computed from the same pre-normalized input as q, k and v, before the output projection. The gate is a bias-free 1536 × 1536 projection per layer, initialized like the query projection and trained by Muon; value embeddings, RoPE and QK-norm are the Dense Baseline's. The gates add 2,359,296 parameters per layer; calibration to the shared budget reduced the depth from 23 to 21 layers and widened the FFN to 6272 (−0.606%).
paperTitle: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
mechanism: G1 gate: Y' = Y ⊙ σ(X W_θ) on each head's attention output, before the output projection
Elementwise, head-specific scores (12 heads × 128 channels) from the pre-normalized block input; no bias
Full causal attention with value embeddings in all 21 layers; FFN 6272
limitations: The paper's results come from a 15B-total MoE and 1.7B dense models trained with AdamW on 400B tokens or more; here the gate trains with Muon on 49B tokens, under a matched compute budget that costs it two of the Dense Baseline's 23 layers. The official code fuses the gate into the query projection; here it is a separate projection computing the same function. The headwise variant (one score per head, about +0.1% compute at the Dense shape) is a plugin option, not this configuration. No formal run yet, so it has no published result. Parameters, memory and speed are outcomes, not controls.
